When fusing Pokemon and determining the potential evolutionary lines, there should always be at least one evolution initially selected from each parent, while all potential evolutionary lines are selected using the 62%/50% weighted priority logic.

When an evolutionary line is selected, the entire line is then available with respect to the following rules.

When evolving, you can only select one Phase 1 and one Phase 2 evolution, if available. If you chose to evolve down the path of one parent's Phase 1 evolution, you cannot then evolve into the other parent's Phase 1 evolution. You could, however, evolve into the other parent's Phase 2 evolution.

As level-up evolutions without additional conditions would contradict each other, we should merge these together into a single evolutionary line. This should come after the initial set of potential evolutions have been selected.

For example, if we were to breed Larvitar with Rattata, we should have one resulting evolutionary line since both parents only have level-up evolutionary lines with no additional conditions. The stage 1 evolution of this line should result in a fusion of both stage 1 evolution of each parent (Raticate and Pupitar). The level this occurs at should be the average of both stage 1 evolutions, rounded up to the nearest whole number. In this example, Rattata evolves into Raticate at level 20, and Larvitar evolves into Pupitar at level 30. Our fused evolutionary line should have it's 1st stage at level 25, and the 2nd stage should occur at level 55 since Pupitar evolves at 55 and Raticate does not have an evolution. This final evolution would be a fusion between the Raticate and Tyranitar.

If there is no change in Pokemon type when an evolution occurs (like when Rattata evolves into Raticate and when Larvitar evolves into Pupitar), there should be no change in the Type 1 and Type 2 of the Berserk Gene profile. If the Type 1 or Type 2 are affected by either parent's evolution, the Berserk Gene Profile should be recalculated for that type respectively.

When a conditional evolution does exist, like with Poliwag, that condition will not be rolled up into the fused evolutionary line. If we were to fuse Poliwag and Dratini, we would have one Phase 1 evolution (a merge of Poliwhirl and Dragonair), that has the optional branches of Dragonite, Poliwrath, and Politoed. If the Dragonite evolution is selected (no item used to evolve into one of the other options), we can't simply fuse that Phase 2 evolution with the other parent's Phase 1 evolution as it would be a weaker option to choose than the other two (which would fuse the selected Phase 2 of the Poliwag line with the level-up Phase 2 of the Dratini line). Instead, we need to create a pseudo-fusion-profile of all of the potential evolutions of the other parent and fuse them with the evolution of the chosen parent. This pseudo-fusion-profile should still use the Type 1, Type 2, and abilities of the currently used phase of the other parent (the one we are creating the pseudo-fusion-profile from, which in our example is Poliwag). We would average the base stats of all evolutionary lines of this parent at this stage, a pseudo-random selection of moves from both parents, and the other factors that we average together just being averaged 50/50. This pseudo-fusion profile will then be merged with the evolution that we chose. So, for our example, if we chose to evolve into Dragonite, the Pokemon we are evolving into is Dragonite fused with the pseudo-fusion of Poliwrath and Politoed. However, if we chose to evolve into Politoed, we are evolving into the fusion of Politoed and Dragonite.
